messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: type argument in unmarkedFrameOccuFP
parts:
Hi;
I'm having trouble finding documentation about using the type argument in unmarkedFrameOccuFP. It appears that it is a vector describing the type of data during each occasion in order from left to right in the data matrix (y). So, if I have data of type 1 (certain detection method, no false positives) for the first 3 occasions and then 2 occasions with a method that might have false detections, I would specify type=c(3,2,0). Would someone please verify if this is this correct? 

If correct, then for a situation in which the certain detection method followed the uncertain in time, I believe it would be necessary to change the order in the data matrix to have the type 1 occasions followed by type 2 - this might make modeling temporal trends challenging!

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: 4b6966f3272cbf59
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] type argument in unmarkedFrameOccuFP
parts:
Hi Eric -

You are correct in how to specify data types. 

As far as temporal trends, occuFP only deals with single season models (Presence and Mark both have multiseason models implemented now). If the interest is temporal trends in detection, then as you note you can not change the order of the data matrix, and instead need to reorder the covariate that will be used to match the temporal order of visits.
